e7_s4_rationale: The presence of bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement on MRI of the hips and pelvis, along with elevated inflammatory markers and the absence of evidence supporting other conditions such as abscess or septic arthritis, supports this diagnosis.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Psoas abscess
e7_s4_rejected.why: No abscess was found on MRI of the lumbar spine or hips and pelvis

e7_s4_rejected.label: Iliopsoas bursitis
e7_s4_rejected.why: While possible, the presence of muscle oedema and systemic inflammation suggests a more diffuse process

e7_s4_rejected.label: Septic arthritis of the hip
e7_s4_rejected.why: Normal MRI of the hip and lack of evidence for infection make this less likely

e7_s4_rejected.label: Polymyalgia rheumatica
e7_s4_rejected.why: While this condition involves inflammation of muscles, the specific involvement of the iliopsoas muscles and the presence of muscle oedema on MRI are more suggestive of idiopathic inflammatory psoas muscle disease

B06_pred: Iliopsoas bursitis or tendinopathy; Gouty arthropathy
B07_pred: Iliopsoas abscess or iliopsoas tendinitis; Insertional tendinopathy of the iliopsoas tendon
